title: 26. Cloud-Native AI/ML & High-Performance Model Serving
summary: Orchestrate distributed deep learning workloads with Kubeflow Training Operator (PyTorchJob) and deploy auto-scaling, low-latency LLM inference pipelines with KServe, Ray, and NVIDIA Triton.
prerequisites: Container resource requests, limits and GPU scheduling
Horizontal Pod Autoscaling (HPA) and Prometheus metrics
learningObjectives: Schedule and monitor distributed multi-worker training jobs using Kubeflow PyTorchJob CRD
Deploy serverless, high-throughput model inference using KServe InferenceService with vLLM runtimes
Configure GPU device plugins, node selectors, tolerations, and resource requests for accelerated compute pods
Scale inference workloads dynamically based on concurrency and queue depth metrics

curriculumModules.title: Kubeflow Training Operator & Distributed PyTorchJob
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Distributed training synchronizes gradients across multiple worker nodes using PyTorch DDP (Distributed Data Parallel) and NCCL. Kubeflow Training Operator coordinates master/worker lifecycle, environment variables, and master service discovery.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Multi-node distributed LLM fine-tuning using PyTorchJob with RDMA/InfiniBand networking and persistent checkpoint storage via Ceph/EFS.

curriculumModules.title: KServe Serverless Model Serving & Hardware Acceleration
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: KServe provides serverless model serving with standardized v2 data plane protocols, scale-to-zero, canary rollouts, and multi-model serving. Integrated with vLLM, HuggingFace, and Triton Inference Server.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: InferenceService deployed on GPU node pool with KServe vLLM predictor, PagedAttention cache, and Knative-based auto-scaling.

labs.title: Distributed Model Training with Kubeflow PyTorchJob
labs.scenario: A data science team requires a distributed training run for a BERT NLP model across 1 master node and 2 distributed worker nodes. Deploy a Kubeflow PyTorchJob custom resource in the kubeflow namespace.
labs.productionContext: Kubeflow PyTorchJob automatically provisions master and worker pods, injects MASTER_ADDR and MASTER_PORT environment variables, and manages distributed training checkpoints.
objectives: Deploy a PyTorchJob named bert-pretrain in the kubeflow namespace
Configure Master replica count to 1 and Worker replica count to 2
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: kubeflow.org/v1
kind: PyTorchJob
metadata:
  name: bert-pretrain
  namespace: kubeflow
spec:
  pytorchReplicaSpecs:
    Master:
      replicas: 1
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: pytorch
              image: kubeflow/pytorch-dist-mnist:v1.0
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "1000m"
                  memory: "2Gi"
    Worker:
      replicas: 2
      restartPolicy: OnFailure
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
            - name: pytorch
              image: kubeflow/pytorch-dist-mnist:v1.0
              resources:
                requests:
                  cpu: "1000m"
                  memory: "2Gi"

labs.title: High-Throughput LLM Serving with KServe InferenceService
labs.scenario: Deploy a high-concurrency LLM inference service using KServe InferenceService with vLLM runtime, minReplicas: 1, and maxReplicas: 5 in the kserve-test namespace.
labs.productionContext: KServe decouples model serving infrastructure from client APIs, supporting serverless auto-scaling and GPU hardware acceleration.
objectives: Configure minReplicas: 1 and maxReplicas: 5 under predictor
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: serving.kserve.io/v1beta1
kind: InferenceService
metadata:
  name: llama-summarizer
  namespace: kserve-test
spec:
  predictor:
    minReplicas: 1
    maxReplicas: 5
    model:
      modelFormat:
        name: vLLM
      storageUri: "s3://kubelabs-models/llama-3-8b-instruct"
      resources:
        requests:
          cpu: "2"
          memory: "8Gi"

assessmentQuestions.question: How does the Kubeflow Training Operator coordinate distributed PyTorch workers?
options: By automatically configuring MASTER_ADDR and MASTER_PORT environment variables and establishing cluster service discovery for the master pod
By restarting the cluster after each epoch
By forcing all workers to write directly to a shared USB drive
By executing single-threaded python scripts sequentially
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Kubeflow Training Operator provisions the Master headless service and injects the network coordinates (MASTER_ADDR/PORT) into all worker containers.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary benefit of KServe InferenceService over standard Kubernetes Deployments for ML serving?
options: Standardized v2 inference protocol, hardware acceleration integration, serverless scale-to-zero, and request-queue-based autoscaling
It eliminates the need for containers
It forces models to run only on CPU
It prevents all incoming HTTP traffic
assessmentQuestions.explanation: KServe abstracts model loading, GPU memory allocation, batching (e.g. vLLM PagedAttention), and auto-scaling based on real-time inference request queues.
